Deactivating secrets risks downtime, X-Ray sampling rules do not filter on Secrets Manager API calls in this way, and CloudWatch alarms on CloudTrail GetSecretValue requests do not identify which secrets are unused.
155: An Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule with a rate(10 minutes) expression invokes the Lambda function on a schedule with no servers to manage. An EC2 cron job is not serverless, a Lambda environment variable is just a value and triggers nothing, and SNS subscriptions have no timer feature.

The Lambda function then gets secretsmanager:GetSecretValue through its role and resolves the secret at runtime using only the secret name from its environment variable. The other options place the plaintext credentials in CloudFormation parameters or Lambda environment variables.
157: Session data must be stored outside the individual instances so that any instance behind the load balancer can serve a user's next request, and ElastiCache provides a fast shared in-memory store for that. EBS volumes attach to a single instance, and instance store and the root filesystem are local and lost when the instance stops or is replaced by Auto Scaling.

X-Forwarded-Proto carries the protocol, X-Forwarded-Port the port, and X-Forwarded-Host the host the client requested, none of which identify the client.

CloudWatch logs lack end-to-end correlation, CloudTrail records API activity for auditing, and Inspector assesses security vulnerabilities.
161: Rolling with additional batch launches an extra batch of instances first and then updates the existing ones in batches, so full capacity is kept throughout and only one extra batch is paid for. All at once causes downtime, while immutable and blue/green keep full capacity but launch an entire second set of instances, which costs more.
162: The AWS SAM CLI runs Lambda functions locally in a container that emulates the Lambda environment: sam local generate-event produces sample events and sam local invoke runs the function against them, so developers can run the tests locally and the same scripts can run in the CI/CD pipeline before the CDK deployment. There is no cdk local invoke command, and a generic unit test framework or custom Node.js Docker container does not reproduce the Lambda environment as closely.
163: The permissions policy already allows read actions on the Cars table in us-west-2, so the Access Denied error means the EC2 instance cannot assume the role. The role needs a trust policy naming the EC2 service principal (ec2.amazonaws.com) so that the instance profile can supply the role credentials. Widening the resource or adding dynamodb:* does not fix an assume-role problem, and the trust relationship should be with EC2, not dynamodb.amazonaws.com.
164: The AWS Encryption SDK uses envelope encryption and stores the encrypted data key in the encryption message it returns together with the ciphertext, so it can later decrypt the data key through the master key provider, such as KMS, without the developer tracking anything. 165: A Lambda execution role is assumed by the function and supplies temporary credentials that rotate automatically, and a policy scoped to the specific S3 objects satisfies least privilege. Hardcoded keys, keys in Secrets Manager and keys in environment variables are all long-term credentials that must be managed and can leak.
166: Granting the CloudFormation service role in each account s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket, and adding a bucket policy that trusts only the specific account numbers as principals, gives cross-account access limited to the intended accounts. A principal of "*" opens the bucket to everyone, and Lambda service-linked roles are not how CloudFormation retrieves the code during stack creation.
167: An Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule that invokes a Lambda function once a day requires no servers, no cluster and no infrastructure management, so it is the most operationally efficient for a small daily task in a new AWS environment. EKS, EC2 with crontab and AWS Batch all require provisioning and maintaining compute infrastructure.

169: ElastiCache for Redis in cluster mode supports encryption at rest and in transit, and replicas with Multi-AZ automatic failover for high availability, so it works as a cache in front of RDS. 170: Adding the X-Amz-Invocation-Type header with the static value Event to the API Gateway integration request makes API Gateway invoke the Lambda function asynchronously, so it returns an immediate 202 response and the function continues processing and can send the email when done. 171: A Lambda layer packages shared libraries once so that all the functions can reference the same layer version, and updating the dependencies means publishing a new layer version instead of repackaging each function. Maintenance windows, runtime upgrades and hosting the dependencies in CodeCommit do not share dependencies among functions.
172: DynamoDB Time to Live deletes expired items automatically and at no cost for the deletes when a Number attribute holds the expiry time as an epoch timestamp, so setting it to 48 hours after creation handles removal with no code or infrastructure. A String or Date attribute is not valid for TTL, and the script and scan-based options consume read and write capacity and compute resources.
173: A Secrets Manager RDS database secret stores the credentials encrypted and has built-in managed rotation for RDS, including SQL Server, with no custom code. Non-secret settings such as the table, bucket and topic names go into Parameter Store SecureString parameters, which can be reused by other applications and updated without code changes. Lambda environment variables are tied to one function, and building custom rotation Lambda functions adds operational overhead.
174: The existing policy only allows read operations, so adding only codecommit:CreateBranch and codecommit:DeleteBranch gives the developer exactly the permissions needed to create and delete branches. Put*, Update* and codecommit:* grant far more than required and violate least privilege.
175: ProvisionedThroughputExceededException is a throttling error, so the application should retry with exponential backoff, and using the AWS SDKs gives that retry-with-backoff behavior built in, unlike hand-built REST API calls. Both are free fixes. Raising throughput, adding DAX, or splitting data across two tables costs more and does not address transient throttling, and DAX helps with reads, not writes.
176: CodeBuild limits the combined size of environment variables, and the recommended fix is to store the values in Systems Manager Parameter Store (or Secrets Manager) and reference them through the parameter-store section of the buildspec, which fetches them at build time. Cognito, S3 settings for environment variables and the LC_ALL locale export are not features that solve this.
177: A Lambda@Edge function can read the dimension and resolution query parameters, resize the original photo on demand, and store the result in S3 so later requests for the same variant are served without reprocessing, and CloudFront caches the responses. Pregenerating variants for hundreds of device sizes with S3 Batch Operations is costly and wasteful, and option C reprocesses images each time they fall out of cache without storing the results.
178: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a fully managed in-memory cache for DynamoDB that reduces read latency from milliseconds to microseconds with only a small change of the endpoint in the application. LSIs do not speed up reads of the same data, S3 Transfer Acceleration is for uploads over distance, and retries with backoff handle throttling instead of lowering latency.
179: To trace requests from an EC2-hosted application, install and configure the AWS X-Ray SDK for Python so the application generates trace segments, and run the X-Ray daemon on the instances to batch and forward those segments to the X-Ray service. The CloudWatch agent and writing logs to arbitrary directories do not produce X-Ray traces.
180: Storing the connection credentials once as a SecureString parameter in Systems Manager Parameter Store, encrypted with KMS, gives all the Lambda functions a single central encrypted source that they read at runtime. IAM database authentication generates per-connection tokens instead of one shared connection string, an RDS instance is not a credentials store, and per-function environment variables do not give a single shared source.
181: Turning on execution logging and access logging for the API stage and pointing it at a CloudWatch Logs log group records request details and the reason API Gateway returned the 400 response, such as validation or mapping failures. CloudTrail records management API calls and not client requests, X-Ray traces latency, and Firehose is not how API Gateway delivers logs.
182: API Gateway stage-level caching can be overridden per method, so you can enable caching for the POST method in the selected stage, and identical requests are then served from the cache using the configured cache keys. The default CloudFront behavior does not cache POST responses, and storing results in the Lambda /tmp directory or Parameter Store is not a proper shared cache.
183: Enabling gradual deployments in the SAM template uses AWS CodeDeploy to shift traffic to the new Lambda version through an alias. Choosing a Canary10Percent30Minutes deployment preference sends only 10 percent of traffic to the new version for 30 minutes before shifting the rest, and pre-traffic and post-traffic hooks run automated tests. A linear preference shifts all traffic in increments rather than testing a small percentage first, and EventInvokeConfig only configures asynchronous destinations.
184: A Secrets Manager secret defined in the CloudFormation template can generate a random password with GenerateSecretString, and a rotation schedule attached to the secret provides automatic rotation, with the application fetching the current value from Secrets Manager. Parameter Store does not generate or rotate passwords, and a custom Lambda resource or cron daemon would need custom code.
185: A Lambda function is not triggered by a DynamoDB stream until an event source mapping connects the stream to the function, which makes Lambda poll the stream and invoke the function with batches of records. 186: For ECS on Fargate, container environment variables are defined in the environment array of the container definition inside the task definition. The service definition does not contain container settings, and entryPoint specifies the executable to run, not environment variables.
187: A DeletionPolicy of Retain on the database resource keeps the database when the resource is removed from the stack or the stack is deleted, and a stack policy that denies updates to the database prevents CloudFormation from replacing it during stack updates. 188: SSE-KMS encrypts S3 objects with a KMS key, and every use of the key is logged in AWS CloudTrail showing which principal used the key and when, which gives the required audit trail. SSE-S3 uses S3-managed keys with no key-use auditing, and SSE-C and self-managed keys do not use KMS at all.
189: A GSI with Product ID as the partition key and Product Rating as the sort key lets you Query for one product with ScanIndexForward set to false and a limit of 10, returning the top-rated reviews directly. 190: CloudFront serving firmware from S3 gives low-cost global distribution with edge caching, and signed URLs restrict downloads to authorized customers for a limited time. A separate distribution per customer, Lambda@Edge, or API Gateway and Lambda in front of S3 each add complexity and cost.
191: For asynchronous Lambda invocations, events that still fail after the configured retries can be sent to a dead-letter queue (SQS or SNS) or an on-failure destination, which preserves the failed event and error context for investigation. CloudTrail does not capture function failure payloads, and SWF and AWS Config are not used to handle unprocessed Lambda events.
192: Aurora PostgreSQL is a PostgreSQL-compatible database, and Secrets Manager has built-in managed rotation for Aurora credentials, so rotation is turned on without writing code. Parameter Store does not offer rotation, and DynamoDB is not PostgreSQL and uses IAM rather than database credentials.
193: Amazon Cognito identity pools can issue temporary AWS credentials to unauthenticated guest users mapped to an IAM role with limited permissions, so no login or user management is needed. Creating IAM users per visitor or distributing KMS-created credentials is insecure and operationally heavy, and an identity provider requires users to authenticate.
194: Before sam deploy, the application must be packaged, in which the code is bundled and uploaded to S3 and the template is transformed to reference it (sam package, or the packaging that sam deploy performs). Manually zipping and uploading to Lambda, testing with X-Ray and using eb create (an Elastic Beanstalk command) are not SAM deployment steps.
195: In the CDK app, the cleanup handler code can be wrapped in a CDK custom resource, which provisions the Lambda function and invokes it as part of stack deployment, so it fits into the existing deployment process with the least configuration. Writing raw CloudFormation JSON, using Amplify APIs, or writing the function in the console and importing it break the integrated CDK flow.
196: Storing the sensitive data as a SecureString parameter in Systems Manager Parameter Store and referencing it with CloudFormation dynamic references keeps the plaintext out of the template, and the value is encrypted with KMS and resolved at deployment. A template parameter would expose the data, and encrypting the template with KMS does not protect parameter values. S3 and EFS storage are not integrated with CloudFormation for this purpose.
197: Secrets Manager stores credentials encrypted with KMS and supports automatic rotation on a schedule for RDS, Aurora and DocumentDB, using rotation Lambda functions based on the AWS rotation templates. Parameter Store has no native automatic rotation, IAM database authentication does not cover DocumentDB the same way and does not provide credential rotation, and S3 server-side encryption key rotation does not rotate database passwords.
198: Lambda scaling opens many database connections and exhausts the Aurora connection limit, and Amazon RDS Proxy pools and shares connections so many Lambda invocations use far fewer database connections. A read replica or Multi-AZ does not solve connection exhaustion on the instance being used, and migrating to DynamoDB is a big redesign.
199: sam local start-api runs a local HTTP server that emulates API Gateway and invokes the Lambda functions locally, so the REST API can be tested locally. sam local invoke runs a single function once, start-lambda emulates the Lambda service endpoint, and generate-event only produces sample event payloads.
200: A Lambda alias can use weighted routing configuration to send a fixed percentage of traffic to a second function version, so the new version is initially available only to that percentage of production users. Canary and linear deployment types are CodeDeploy deployment configurations and not part of the in-house deployment solution, and environment variables cannot route traffic between versions.
201: ElastiCache for Memcached is a multi-threaded, horizontally scalable caching engine that can offload read traffic from RDS and fits the stated multi-threaded requirement. Redis is single-threaded for command execution, DAX only works with DynamoDB, and the standby instance of a Multi-AZ RDS deployment cannot serve read traffic.
202: Lambda environment variables are encrypted at rest, and using a KMS customer managed key keeps the API key encrypted at rest with controlled access to the key. Prompting a user fails for a scheduled function, hardcoding the key in code leaves it in plaintext, and Lambda@Edge with HTTPS does not address encryption at rest.
203: S3 Standard-IA stores data across multiple Availability Zones for resiliency at a lower cost than Standard, and Glacier Deep Archive standard retrieval completes within 12 hours, which meets the 24-hour requirement. Intelligent-Tiering has monitoring fees that are not worthwhile for rarely accessed data.
204: The SAM CLI configuration file (samconfig.toml) can contain a separate table for each environment, and sam deploy --config-env selects the environment's parameters, so one template deploys to dev, test and staging with minimal effort. Maintaining multiple templates or custom scripts is more work, and parameter overrides alone do not capture the full per-environment configuration.
205: Adding an S3 trigger to the Lambda function configures an S3 event notification for object-created events on the bucket, which invokes the function immediately after each upload. Asynchronous invocation is an invocation type and not a source, EventBridge is not how the trigger is added here, and a layer only packages libraries and code.
206: By default CloudFormation rolls back and deletes resources created so far when a create fails. The --disable-rollback option on create-stack and update-stack keeps the successfully provisioned resources for troubleshooting. Termination protection prevents stack deletion, and parameters or tags named PreserveResources have no effect on rollback behavior.
207: Amazon RDS Proxy maintains a pool of database connections and multiplexes the connections from many Lambda invocations onto it, reducing database load without limiting Lambda scaling. Provisioned and reserved concurrency control Lambda concurrency and either keep functions warm or cap scaling, and Aurora cluster cache management is a failover cache feature and is not a connection endpoint.
208: Branching from main into one branch for production bug fixes and another for the new version's development lets both lines of work proceed independently and be merged later, which is the standard Git workflow in CodeCommit. Tags are fixed pointers and not places to commit ongoing work, a separate repository fragments the history, and an IAM policy that blocks pushes to the production branch would prevent the fixes the developer needs to deploy.
209: When a template creates IAM resources with custom names, CloudFormation requires acknowledgment through the CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM capability. Using an administrator role does not remove the capability acknowledgment requirement.
210: A client can invalidate an API Gateway cache entry by sending a request with the Cache-Control: max-age=0 header, provided the caller's IAM policy grants execute-api:InvalidateCache on the API. InvalidateCache is not a management API operation customers call, and INVALIDATE_CACHE is not a valid query string parameter.
211: Every Lambda function gets ephemeral storage in the /tmp directory (512 MB by default, configurable up to 10,240 MB), which is more than enough for 100 MB and is scoped to the execution environment, so it needs no extra service or cost. 212: The Lambda function already processes the stream records, so once its execution role can write to CloudWatch Logs (AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole) the logged orders can be analyzed with a CloudWatch Logs Insights query that filters quantity = 0, uses count_distinct(customerId) and bins by 1d. 213: Security groups are stateful and the connection is initiated by the function, so the function's security group needs outbound access on port 1433 to the database and the DB instance's security group needs inbound access on 1433 from the function's security group. 214: aws ec2 run-instances launches new EC2 instances from an AMI with the specified instance type, key pair and networking. start-instances only restarts an existing stopped instance, bundle-instance is a legacy command for creating an instance-store AMI from a Windows instance, and confirm-product-instance checks whether a product code is attached to an instance.
215: AWS CloudFormation lets you define infrastructure as templates, deploy the same template repeatedly to create identical stacks, preview changes with change sets, and roll back to a previous state. Storing those templates in AWS CodeCommit gives version control so earlier versions can be restored. OpsWorks with cost reports, CloudWatch metrics with tagging, and Elastic Beanstalk do not provide repeatable, versioned, stageable infrastructure definitions across arbitrary AWS resources.
216: UpdateItem is an upsert in DynamoDB: it modifies the specified attributes of an existing item and creates the item if the key does not exist, GetItem retrieves the item, and PutItem allows creating or replacing it. UpdateItem, GetItem and PutItem together cover the retrieve, update and create behavior. The other sets include DeleteItem, DescribeTable, UpdateTable (which changes table settings) or GetRecords (a stream/Kinesis API), and none of them supply UpdateItem for partial attribute changes.
217: With a cache placed in front of DynamoDB, a lazy-loading (cache-aside) pattern keeps serving the cached price until the entry expires or is explicitly invalidated, so updates written to DynamoDB are not visible. Invalidating or updating the cache entry when the price changes, or using a short TTL, fixes this. A write-through cache would actually keep the cache current, and insufficient read or write capacity would cause throttling errors rather than stale-but-successful reads.
218: The AWS SDK default credential provider chain checks environment variables before the instance profile credentials from the instance metadata service. The application still has the old access key variables set, belonging to the deleted IAM user, so the SDK uses them and DynamoDB rejects the calls. Removing the environment variables lets the SDK fall through to the role credentials. The SDK fully supports instance roles, a security group does not filter calls to the link-local metadata address, and IAM changes propagate within seconds, not a long time. The CLI works because the developer uses personal credentials.
219: AWS Secrets Manager supports multi-Region secret replication, which keeps a read-only replica of the secret (encrypted with a KMS key in the target Region) in the secondary Region so the application can fetch it by Region-specific ARN during failover, and it removes hardcoded credentials securely. Parameter Store has no built-in cross-Region replication, and plaintext config files in S3 with CRR or on EFS keep credentials in files that are less secure and not designed for secret management.
220: A ThrottlingException from the CloudWatch API means the request rate exceeded the API limits for the account, and the standard best practice is to retry with exponential backoff (with jitter), which the AWS SDKs support natively. Calls are intermittent so backing off will let later retries succeed. Asking for a limit increase is not the first step, the CLI is subject to the same API throttling, and removing the call would lose the data the application needs.
221: An Application Load Balancer terminates the client connection and opens a new one to the target, so the application sees the ALB's address as the source. The ALB adds an X-Forwarded-For header containing the original client IP (and any proxy IPs appended in a comma-separated list), so changing the application to parse that header keeps horizontal scaling at the lowest cost. Removing the load balancer gives up scaling, a Classic Load Balancer is not needed because the header solves the problem, and requiring clients to send a custom header is unreliable and spoofable.
222: An SNS FIFO topic fanning out to SQS FIFO queues preserves ordering and deduplicates by message group, so both the inventory and payment consumers see orders in the order they were received, which lets the first order claim the seat and a rejected payment pass the seat to the next order. Standard SNS topics and standard SQS queues give only best-effort ordering and at-least-once delivery. Chaining the Lambda functions sequentially removes the parallel processing and does not provide ordering across concurrent requests.
223: In AWS X-Ray, annotations are key-value pairs that are indexed, so they can be used in filter expressions and groups to search traces by custom attributes. Metadata is not indexed and cannot be used in filter expressions, arbitrary new segment fields are not allowed by the segment document schema, and sampling rules control how many requests are traced by service, URL, or method, not how results are filtered afterwards.
224: Kinesis Data Streams supports server-side encryption using AWS KMS, which encrypts data before it is stored in the stream's storage layer and decrypts it when consumers read, so records are protected at rest for the retention period. SSL/TLS only protects data in transit, the Kinesis Client Library does not encrypt stored data, and a Lambda function could only encrypt after the data is already stored unencrypted.
225: Kinesis Data Streams is built for real-time ingestion of very high volumes of events and lets multiple consumers read the same shards concurrently (shared throughput or enhanced fan-out), and it is the cheapest way to handle millions of events per day with several consumers. SNS with SQS queues per application (standard or FIFO) multiplies per-message charges and FIFO throughput is limited, and Kinesis Data Firehose is a delivery service to destinations such as S3 and is not intended for multiple custom consumers processing the data in real time.
226: The template defines a bucket and an output with a !Ref to it. There is no Exported property on resources or an ImportResource function, Fn::Include is not a way to reuse resources from another stack, and a custom resource would add needless complexity.
227: ProvisionedThroughputExceededException on writes means the table's write capacity is too low for the burst of requests, so switching the table to on-demand capacity mode removes the need to size throughput in advance and absorbs the traffic. The application should also retry with exponential backoff, which reduces the request rate during throttling and is the recommended practice that the SDK follows. Increasing RCUs does not help writes, a larger instance would only send more requests faster, and shortening the retry delay makes throttling worse.
228: An S3 presigned URL grants time-limited access to a specific object without sharing credentials or making the bucket public, and a URL signed with IAM user credentials can be valid for up to 7 days (604,800 seconds), which matches the workshop window. 229: A single API Gateway REST API supports multiple stages (dev, test, prod) with stage variables, and each stage can point to a different Lambda alias of one Lambda function (for example dev, test, prod aliases mapped to versions). Separate APIs and functions per environment or per Region multiply the resources, and passing the environment in a REST parameter is insecure and does not isolate the environments.
230: When a Lambda function is registered as an ALB target, the ALB needs a resource-based policy on the function that lets elasticloadbalancing.amazonaws.com invoke it. Lambda can be an ALB target through both the console and CLI, and cross-zone load balancing is irrelevant to Lambda targets.
231: AWS Secrets Manager stores secrets encrypted with AWS KMS and has built-in managed rotation for Amazon RDS credentials, using a rotation Lambda function that updates both the secret and the database password on a schedule. Lambda environment variables cannot rotate automatically, Parameter Store SecureString parameters do not offer managed rotation, and X-Amz-Security-Token is the header for STS session tokens, not a place to keep database credentials.
232: A Lambda alias can point to two function versions and split invocation traffic between them by weight (for example 90 percent to the current version and 10 percent to the new one), which gives a controlled canary-style test of the new version. 233: Lambda limits the unzipped deployment package to 250 MB including layers, and this is a hard limit that cannot be raised with a quota request. Zipping repeatedly or using a different compression algorithm does not change the unzipped size, and the limit is not adjustable through Support.
234: Setting maximum concurrency on the SQS event source mapping limits how many concurrent Lambda invocations are made from the queue, so the rate of calls to the third-party API can be kept under its documented limit and messages are not rejected with 429 errors. Increasing the batch size increases the work per invocation without reducing request rate, provisioned concurrency only pre-warms environments and does not limit concurrency, and asynchronous invocation retry settings do not apply to SQS event source mappings.
235: The workload is read heavy and the RDS instance's read latency is rising at peak, so caching frequently read query results in Amazon ElastiCache (Redis or Memcached) offloads reads from the database and reduces latency. Adding ECS instances or task memory scales the application tier but the bottleneck is the database, and RCUs are a DynamoDB concept that does not exist for RDS instances.
236: The application needs only to list the bucket and download objects, so the policy should allow s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN (arn:aws:s3:::DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET) and s3:GetObject on the object ARN (DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET/*), which is exactly option A. Option B grants s3:* on objects, option C also allows PutObject and DeleteObject, and option D denies GetObject, which would block the downloads.
237: Creating a data key in AWS KMS gives a plaintext key for local symmetric encryption and an encrypted copy to store with the file, and the AWS Encryption SDK implements envelope encryption on the client side with these keys, so encryption happens inside the application before upload. An HMAC key is used to generate and verify message authentication codes and not to encrypt, a data key pair is asymmetric, and the AWS CLI cannot perform client-side encryption of files inside the application with a KMS data key.
238: An IAM role with a least-privilege policy for the specific S3 actions, attached to the EC2 instance through an instance profile, gives the application temporary credentials that are rotated automatically and never stored on disk. IAM user access keys in environment variables are long-lived secrets, roles do not have access keys, and an S3 bucket policy cannot grant access based on an EC2 instance ID.
239: An Application Load Balancer HTTPS listener supports a built-in authenticate-cognito action in listener rules, which redirects unauthenticated users to the Cognito user pool, and setting OnUnauthenticatedRequest to deny rejects requests that are not authenticated with an HTTP 401. Checking only for a missing Authorization header does not validate it, adding API Gateway in front of the ALB is extra infrastructure, and a Lambda target group would not sit in front of the existing targets to validate tokens.
240: Throttling happens when a function reaches its concurrency limit, so raising the function's reserved concurrency (provided unreserved account concurrency is available) guarantees more concurrent executions for that function, and requesting an account-level concurrency quota increase raises the total pool available. Migrating to EKS is a major change, increasing the maximum event age only affects how long asynchronous events are retried, and the lambda:GetFunctionConcurrency permission only lets someone read the setting.
241: API Gateway stages are designed for multiple deployments of the same API, each stage with its own invoke URL, and stage variables can pass the version or Lambda alias context to the backend.
